title: If you can’t ship a playable demo this weekend, the bottleneck isn’t talent
author: pataderushikesh
selftext:
I built a playable game without Unity, Godot, Unreal, or a CS degree.

No asset store. No “just one more tutorial.” No 47 abandoned repos.

Type what you want → play it in the browser → share the link.

Gatekeepers will call it fake.  
Players will just… play. 

Try mine: [https://app-ludexel.rushour0.com/play/JllECRU4lug](https://app-ludexel.rushour0.com/play/JllECRU4lug)

If this makes you angry, ask yourself why unfinished projects feel safer than shipping.

  
[https://blogs.rushour0.com/building-the-engine-and-the-product/](https://blogs.rushour0.com/building-the-engine-and-the-product/) this is how I am building this setup lmk how you like the blog or the game. ( NO MONEY OR ANYTHING TO BE PAID ANYWHERE )

comments.author: Visible_Software_902
comments.body: The mgba loader seems broken, and requires a hard refresh to fix (incorrect fetch handler?). Don't see much point building this for a 25+ year old platform unless you're planning to make retro carts and run it on hardware. Most people bothering with GBA today do it for modding or as a learning exercise, and the latter kind of loses its purpose if an agent is writing everything anyways.

replies.author: promptling
replies.body: Getting people to actually click Play is often harder than building the demo, especially before it has any social proof. Full disclosure: I’m building [Patchloop](https://patchloop.io/) specifically for agentically built games in progress—a place to recruit playtesters, run feedback loops, and keep a dedicated room around each game instead of starting from zero after every Reddit post. Ludexel feels exactly like the kind of experiment it’s meant for.
